purpose:
A single-user macOS dictation application. It captures speech, recognizes it, optionally rewrites it under a user-selected mode, and inserts the result into the application the user was working in. Every speech and language operation runs on the user's Mac. There is no cloud fallback, no account, no subscription gate, and no artificial cap on recording length or usage; the limits are the hardware and the models the user installs.

In scope: recording controls, text delivery, recording display, built-in modes, custom modes, automatic mode selection, vocabulary, context, languages, input sources, meetings, history, models, desktop behavior. Out of scope: cloud inference, account-based settings synchronization, paywalls, enterprise billing and authentication, and any Windows or iOS client.

The whole product is designed before implementation work is cut, because several requirements constrain the persistence schema, the process model and the ingest boundary in ways that are expensive to retrofit: re-recognizing old audio through a different speech model while keeping every derived artifact attributable (D-029), deleting a recording while a worker is producing a result for it (D-024, D-033), snapshotting mode settings so a later edit cannot change the meaning of a saved result (D-006), recovering a crash at any stage without duplicating delivered text (D-010, D-031), and bounding memory on a multi-hour import across a process boundary (D-018). Left to whichever implementation task first encounters them, those force the schema and the job model into a shape that cannot express them.

Five things the reviewed design left open or wrong are settled here. Inference runs in bundled XPC services whose sandbox withholds the network entitlement (D-003, D-028), so the offline property is enforced by the operating system instead of inferred from a symbol scan; the follow-up inspection in ref/RESEARCH.md points at that mechanism and states that a socket-symbol scan cannot establish that a process lacks network access. The speech runtime (D-020) and the diarizer (D-023) are chosen on the available evidence, and the measurements that would evaluate those choices are stated separately from the choices and remain unperformed. Derived text hangs off identified processing runs (D-029). Captured audio is journaled in independently recoverable chunks (D-030). Recovery, permission loss and retention each have a state-indexed contract (D-031, D-032, D-033) in place of one global rule.

Three review objections are answered in a form different from the one proposed, for reasons recorded with the decisions. No design can guarantee that text found on screen never influences a generated result, so D-012 states the invariants that are checkable, fails closed when they cannot be checked in the run's language, and bounds the claim to those invariants. Withdrawing speaker separation until a diarizer proves out would drop a requested feature, so D-023 names the diarizer, represents absent calibration as unknown, and keeps manual assignment available when the model's evidence is weak. Deleting media resume would give up behavior the specification asks for, so D-025 keeps the pause, makes resume a user action by default, and states what the app can observe about ownership and what it cannot.

The historical feature inventories from the mcwhisper and super experiments are evidence about desired scope. Their generated plans and dependency choices do not bind this design.

## Layering rule

One rule governs dependency direction. DictationCore depends only on DictationPorts; adapters depend on DictationPorts and on system frameworks; nothing depends on an adapter except the composition root in the app shell. DictationCore contains no AppKit, no AVFoundation, no SQLite and no XPC code, so the run state machine, mode resolution, the vocabulary pipeline, prompt assembly, output validation and scheduling policy can be exercised without a microphone, a model or a window server.

## Package and target layout (D-002)

A Swift Package Manager package, LocalDictation, with library targets:

- DictationPorts: protocols and value types shared by core and adapters (AudioSource, AudioFrame, SpeechRecognizer, TextGenerator, Diarizer, DecoderProvider, TextInserter, FocusObserver, ContextProvider, ModelStore, RecordingStore, LeaseBroker, ShortcutRegistrar, MediaController, RuntimeCapabilityDescriptor).
- DictationCore: run state machine, RunManifest assembly, mode resolution, vocabulary pipeline, prompt assembly, ResourceScheduler policy, delivery policy.
- TextValidation: transformation contracts, validator checks, per-language validator packs covering segmentation, interrogative detection and content-word extraction.
- DictationStore: SQLite schema, migrations, repositories, the audio chunk journal and its sealer, tombstones, generations, the lease broker.
- AudioIngest: AVAudioEngine microphone source, ScreenCaptureKit system-audio source, AVAssetReader seekable file source, converters to the canonical recognition format.
- SpeechRuntimeWhisperKit, plus SpeechRuntimeWhisperCpp when Intel coverage is required (D-020); DiarizerSpeakerKit; LanguageRuntimeLlamaCpp. Each publishes a RuntimeCapabilityDescriptor.
- InferenceIPC: message types and the connection client shared by the app and the services.
- SystemIntegration: accessibility insertion, pasteboard, CGEventTap shortcuts, media control, status item, permission probes.
- DictationUI: SwiftUI views, recording panel, settings, history browser.

Four bundled XPC services carry the code that must not reach the network: SpeechService, GenerationService and DecodeService, plus ModelDownloader, which is the only one that may. Each service is a thin main over a library target, so swift test covers its logic. The Xcode app target produces the bundles and owns entitlements, hardened runtime, privacy usage strings and notarization, none of which is expressible in Package.swift.

## Process model (D-003, D-028)

The app shell runs unsandboxed, because setting selected text in other applications and running a session-level event tap are unavailable to a sandboxed application outside the Mac App Store. Each inference service is sandboxed on its own and its entitlement set omits com.apple.security.network.client, so an outbound connection is denied by the system whatever the linked code contains. Model files reach a service as opened file descriptors, or through a read-only path exception scoped to Models/blobs for a runtime that insists on opening a model directory by path; which of the two applies is the output of gate F2. Audio crosses the connection in bounded windows under the credit protocol of D-018.

Nothing listens on a TCP port. A local HTTP endpoint would bind a port every process on the machine can reach, would need its own authentication, and is the component most likely to acquire forwarding behavior through configuration the app does not own; RESEARCH raises that for llama.cpp's server tooling.

ModelDownloader holds the network entitlement, an allowlist of model hosts, and write access confined to Models/.staging. It runs only on explicit user action, and no inference service can start it.

A service can fail or be terminated independently of its client, so connection interruption is a first-class event. The run fails at its current stage, committed results stand, and the next admission loads the model into a fresh service. A service holds only state the app can rebuild from the run manifest and the store: one loaded model, the current job's window queue, and that job's decoder state.

## Processing runs (D-029)

A recording owns audio artifacts. Every piece of derived text belongs to a processing_run, which pins the settings that produced it and names its entry stage. Runs come in four kinds: dictation, covering capture through delivery; import; reprocess_recognition, which re-runs recognition over stored audio; and reprocess_text, which re-runs refining, rewriting, translation or notes over a named earlier result. Only dictation runs may deliver text.

## The lifetime of a dictation run (D-006)

Component boundaries follow this sequence.

1. idle.
2. arming, budgeted at 200 ms: resolve the effective mode from the automatic-selection rules (D-014); latch the delivery target, meaning frontmost process id, bundle identifier, window number, focused accessibility element and whether that element supports settable selected text (D-008); sample context sources in parallel against the budget (D-016); assemble a RunManifest naming mode revision, speech model installation, language model installation, vocabulary revision, language setting, translation flag and validator language pack; allocate a UUIDv7 recording id and run id; create the session directory; write and fsync manifest v0.
3. capturing: the audio source delivers timestamped native frames; a writer task appends them to the chunk journal (D-030) and feeds the provisional recognizer; the panel shows live text and an envelope (D-011).
4. sealing: stop the source, encode the journal into the library artifact, fsync, then commit the recording row, artifact row and run row in one transaction. That is the first point at which the recording exists in History.
5. recognizing: one pass over the complete audio produces a recognition result with segment timings and per-segment average log-probability. The provisional stream is discarded instead of promoted; it was computed over partial context and is a different artifact.
6. refining: deterministic vocabulary replacement and optional filler removal produce a normalized result derived from that recognition result (D-015).
7. rewriting, only when the mode has a generation stage: prompt assembly, generation in the service, contract validation (D-012).
8. delivering: exactly one attempt, guarded by a committed idempotency record (D-010).
9. terminal: complete, cancelled(stage), failed(stage, reason), or delivery_unresolved.

Imports enter at capturing with a seekable source and no delivery latch. Meetings enter at capturing with two sources and continue to a notes run in place of delivery. Reprocessing enters at recognizing or refining with a manifest that names the parent result. One machine serves every input source and every reprocessing path, which is why cancellation, recovery and deletion each have a single definition.

## Concurrency and ownership (D-004)

One RunActor per processing run owns that run's state, rows and files, and is the only writer for them. Two runs on the same recording are serialized by the recording's lease (D-033). The audio callback thread never touches an actor, allocates or locks; it writes frames and a 10 ms RMS and peak envelope into two lock-free rings.

A single ResourceScheduler actor admits model-bound work in three lanes. Capture is never queued. The interactive lane covers the provisional pass and the recognition and rewrite for the run the user is waiting on. The batch lane covers imports, meeting notes and reprocessing. At most one speech job and one generation job hold a loaded model at a time (D-027). Whether an admitted batch job can be preempted is read from the runtime's measured capability descriptor, which records cancellation latency, whether a window boundary is a safe checkpoint, and whether resuming from a checkpoint reproduces the unpreempted transcript. A runtime reporting safe checkpoints yields at the next window; one that does not is cancelled and restarted from its last committed checkpoint, or allowed to finish behind a bound the panel displays. Until descriptors exist the scheduler uses cancel-and-restart, which is correct for both cases and slower for one.

## Component responsibilities

- ModeResolver (core): a pure function from foreground application, URL when readable, explicit override and the ordered rule list to a mode revision.
- VocabularyPipeline (core): pure text-to-text with an explicit stage order and ICU-based segmentation.
- PromptAssembler (core): mode instructions, then context fenced with a per-run random delimiter and labeled as reference material, then the normalized transcript, then the task line restated.
- ContractValidator (TextValidation): checks generated text against the mode's structured transformation contract in the run's language and decides among accept, retry once, and fall back to the normalized transcript.
- DeliveryCoordinator (core policy) with TextInserter (adapter): focus and insertion policy separated from insertion mechanism, so policy is testable without a window server.
- RecordingStore with LeaseBroker (DictationStore): the only writers of History rows and library files, and the enforcement point for tombstones, generations and leases for every writer including retention.
- InferenceClient (InferenceIPC): connection lifecycle, credit accounting, interruption handling, per-service residency accounting.

## Why this supports the whole scope as capabilities land

The run state machine, the manifest snapshot, the provenance graph, the recovery table and the lease protocol are built first against fake adapters. Every later capability adds an adapter behind an existing port, a result kind such as translation or notes, or a validator language pack. None of them changes how a run is recorded, cancelled, recovered or deleted. The parts that are expensive to change late are exercised against fakes, where cancel-at-every-stage and kill-at-every-boundary suites are cheap to run.

## Stores and ownership

DictationStore owns everything under ~/Library/Application Support/LocalDictation/:

```
library.sqlite                                  metadata, runs, results, FTS index (WAL)
Recordings/<uuid>/manifest.json
Recordings/<uuid>/journal/<stream>/<seq>.pcm    durable capture chunks
Recordings/<uuid>/journal/<stream>/index.log    packet index for sealing
Recordings/<uuid>/audio/<stream>.caf            sealed library artifact
Recordings/<uuid>/source/<original filename>    imported original
Models/blobs/<sha256>/                          immutable verified installs
Models/.staging/<uuid>/                         in-flight downloads and imports
Scratch/<jobId>/                                service temporaries
```

One writer connection in WAL mode; readers use separate connections. RunActor never writes SQLite directly. It calls repository methods that enforce tombstone, generation and lease rules.

## Provenance graph (D-029)

- recordings(id, created_at, source_kind, duration_ms, interrupted, deleted_at, generation, audio_state, display_run_id)
- audio_artifacts(id, recording_id, role, path, container, codec, sample_rate, channels, sealed_at, sha256, byte_length), role in {microphone, system, imported_original}
- processing_runs(id, recording_id, recording_generation, kind, entry_stage, parent_result_id, manifest_json, state, started_at, ended_at, reason)
- results(id, run_id, recording_id, kind, derived_from_result_id, text, params_json, created_at), kind in {recognition, normalized, rewritten, translation, notes}
- segments, speaker_clusters, speaker_identities, speaker_assignments, modes, mode_revisions, vocabulary_revisions, rules, model_installations, model_assets, active_models, leases, context_digests, delivery_attempts, delivery_profiles, jobs

Every result names its immediate input. A recognition result has derived_from_result_id NULL and roots its run's chain; normalized derives from recognition; rewritten derives from normalized; a translation derives from whichever result the user translated. A recording can hold several recognition results, one per recognition run, each carrying the speech model installation that produced it. The source transcript is therefore a property of a run, and the question of which transcript a rewrite used is answered by a foreign key instead of by inference from timestamps. Results are immutable after insert, enforced by a trigger that rejects UPDATE on results.text; reprocessing inserts and never replaces. recordings.display_run_id is a user-movable pointer deciding what the list view shows.

## Persistence choice (D-005)

SQLite through GRDB with FTS5 over result text. History search is a stated requirement and FTS5 with bm25 ranking and snippets is why SQLite wins here; SwiftData and Core Data have no comparable text index and their migration behavior is harder to test against fixtures. Schema versions are numbered migrations, each with a test that runs the migration against a fixture database captured at the prior version.

## Audio: journal, sealing and artifacts (D-030)

Capture writes fixed-period chunks, two seconds by default, of raw interleaved Int16 at the source's native rate into journal/<stream>/. Each chunk is written to <seq>.pcm.part, fsynced, renamed to <seq>.pcm, and the directory is fsynced. A chunk carries no header; its format lives in the fsynced manifest, so any complete chunk decodes on its own and a torn final chunk is discardable. A sealer running in the batch lane encodes completed chunks into Apple Lossless in CAF, appends chunk sequence, packet count and byte offset to index.log with an fsync, and deletes chunks whose packets are durably recorded, keeping transient journal storage near a 30-second window instead of the whole recording. At the end of capture the sealer writes the CAF packet table from index.log, fsyncs, records the artifact sha256, and the run commits.

The design does not assume a truncated container can be finalized. After a crash, recovery rebuilds the packet table from index.log up to the last durable entry, truncates the container to that extent, and appends surviving chunks. Worst-case loss is the unsealed tail: at most one chunk period plus data the operating system had not yet flushed within it. The exact bound comes from the kill-at-offset experiment described under verification, which has not been run; the chunk period is the tuning knob if the measurement is worse than expected.

Canonical recognition format is 16 kHz mono Float32, produced by a converter stage after the ingest port instead of at the source. Sealed dictation audio is 16 kHz mono ALAC at roughly 50 to 60 MB per hour, by arithmetic from 16-bit PCM at 115 MB per hour; meeting streams are sealed at native rate, which is larger and is reported in the library size view. Lossy encoding is rejected because re-recognition with a better model later is a requirement. Imported files are copied in their original encoding and decoded on demand.

## Model installations and their notices (D-022)

model_installations records identity (publisher, revision string, sha256 over the ordered weight file set), runtime kind, declared capabilities, install time and origin. model_assets records one row per weight file with its own sha256, size, license identifier and the path of the retained notice text. RESEARCH observes that a development kit's license does not describe every model a user might import, and that the public diarization collection carries component-specific notices; recording the notice per asset is what lets the model manager state terms for the exact weights installed. The application bundles no weights.

## Settings snapshots and derived results

A mode is a named entity with an append-only chain of mode_revisions, each content-addressed over prompt, formatting rules, transformation contract, validator language list and model selections. A run's manifest stores revision identifiers. Editing a mode creates a revision and leaves saved results pointing at the revision that produced them, which makes the requirement that later edits must not silently change a saved result structural instead of procedural. History shows the producing revision and diffs it against the current one.

## Context retention (D-016)

By default the store keeps a SHA-256 digest, byte length and source kind per context sample in context_digests, and not the text. That is enough to tell a user reprocessing an old recording that the original context is unavailable, without retaining copies of unrelated documents and screens. Retaining the text is opt-in per mode, shown in History, and deleted with the recording.

## Interrupted operations (D-031)

The ordering rule is stated once: an externally visible irreversible effect is preceded by a durable record of intent, which is what delivery does, while a local idempotent effect is followed by its commit, which is what sealing does. Recovery at launch reconciles manifests, files and rows by run state.

- arming: remove the session directory. No rows.
- capturing: seal the journal, commit the recording with interrupted set, mark the run cancelled(capturing, crash). Nothing was delivered; History offers recognition.
- sealing: a sealed artifact may exist without rows. Re-sealing is idempotent because it derives from the journal and index.log, so recovery completes it and commits as above.
- recognizing: no partial transcript is saved; the run becomes failed(recognizing, interrupted); audio is retained; History offers a new recognition run.
- refining: the recognition result is committed and immutable, and refining is a pure function of committed inputs pinned in the manifest, so recovery re-runs it, commits the normalized result and stops.
- rewriting: the run becomes failed(rewriting, interrupted); the normalized result stands; History offers a rewrite run. Recovery never resumes generation.
- delivering: any delivery_attempts row in pending, posted or posted_unconfirmed becomes needs_review, the run becomes delivery_unresolved, and nothing is re-posted (D-010).
- Scratch directories, staged model directories and model blobs with no referencing row and no live lease are removed. Leases with no live holder are reclaimed.

## Deletion during active processing (D-024, D-033)

Deletion sets recordings.deleted_at, increments recordings.generation, and signals cancellation to every lease holder. Each worker carries recording id and generation from admission. A worker's commit is one transaction that re-reads the recording row and aborts if the row is missing, tombstoned or at a different generation; on abort it removes its scratch directory and returns. The existence check and the insert cannot be separated, so a late response cannot recreate a deleted recording, and the generation counter covers delete-then-recreate at the same identifier.

Hard deletion of rows, artifacts and FTS entries runs when the last lease on the recording is released, and again at launch. Until then the recording is hidden and reported as deleting instead of as reclaimed space.

## Retention (D-033)

Retention defaults to keeping everything. Optional age-based, size-based and audio-discarding policies are ordinary deletion jobs: they acquire the same leases, observe the same generation checks, and skip any recording with a live lease held by a worker, a player or an export, retrying on the next pass. Discarding audio moves recordings.audio_state to audio_discarded, which History displays; playback and re-recognition are then unavailable while text reprocessing remains available. The first run of any policy lists exactly what it would remove before removing it.

## Cancellation by run stage (D-007)

Cancellation has a defined effect at every stage and the panel names that effect when it happens. Cancelling one run never alters results committed by another run.

- arming: nothing captured; session directory removed; no rows.
- capturing: capture stops; the journal is discarded by default and no History row is created; a per-mode setting seals it as an interrupted recording instead.
- recognizing: the worker stops at its next checkpoint; audio is kept; the run is marked cancelled; no partial transcript is saved, because a truncated transcript that looks complete is worse than none.
- refining: the recognition result stands; the normalized result is dropped.
- rewriting: generation stops; the normalized result is kept and offered for delivery.
- delivering: cancellable until the first event is posted. After that the app reports that delivery was attempted and stops; it does not try to undo keystrokes in another application.

## Permissions as a capability matrix (D-032)

Revocation is handled per capability and per run state in place of one global rule. Losing a capability terminates only the work that capability serves.

- Microphone denied at launch: recording controls disabled with a link to the settings pane; file import still works. Revoked during capturing: capture stops, the journal is sealed, the recording is marked interrupted, nothing is delivered.
- Screen Recording denied: system audio and screen context unavailable; microphone recording, all modes, and rules that do not need screen context continue; meetings degrade to microphone only with a visible marker. Revoked during capturing of a meeting: the system stream ends and is marked truncated at a timestamp, the microphone stream continues, and the recording states which streams cover which interval.
- Accessibility denied or revoked: selected-text insertion is unavailable and delivery falls back to the pasteboard path or to a held result; recognition and rewriting continue to completion. Revocation during recognizing does not stop recognition.
- Input Monitoring denied or revoked: the event tap cannot run, so push-to-talk is unavailable and toggle falls back to a Carbon hotkey; an in-flight run continues and the panel gains a stop control.
- Automation for a browser denied: URL predicates do not match, rule evaluation continues, and the panel shows that the mode came from the fallback.
- Restoration: capabilities are re-probed on the relevant system notification and at each arming, and the panel reports a recovered capability once instead of on every session.

## Secure input

If IsSecureEventInputEnabled() is true at arming, the run records but is marked delivery-unavailable up front. If it becomes true by delivery time, the app posts no events, holds the result in History, offers copy, and states that another application has secure input active. Password fields are the common case, and silently dropping text there would be the worst available failure.

## Delivery failures (D-008, D-009, D-010)

Insertion is defined in terms of caret and selection. The first rung sets AXSelectedText on the latched element, which inserts at the caret or replaces the user's selection; the app never sets AXValue, because RESEARCH records that setting an editable field's value can replace its contents. Rungs are chosen from a capability probe taken at arming and re-checked at delivery.

- Selected-text insertion unsupported, or the probe fails: fall to the pasteboard path.
- Pasteboard path with readable target state, meaning value length or selected-text range: sample before and after Command-V and wait up to 500 ms for a change. Observed change means delivered. Observed absence of change means rejected, and only then is synthesized Unicode typing attempted, capped at 400 characters, above which the app holds and offers copy.
- Pasteboard path with unreadable target state: the outcome is unobservable, since posting a paste event carries no acknowledgment that the target consumed the pasteboard. The attempt is recorded posted_unconfirmed, nothing is retried, and the panel offers Copy and Deliver again as user actions. Synthetic typing is never used after an unobservable outcome, since that is how a paragraph gets inserted twice.
- Pasteboard restore: attempted after the outcome is determined, never on a fixed timer relative to the paste, and only while changeCount still equals ours. For unobservable outcomes the restore is deferred by a per-application profile delay, 750 ms by default, and the panel offers Restore now. Applications measured to read the pasteboard late have restore disabled in their profile, with the panel stating that the dictated text is still on the pasteboard.
- Pasteboard cannot be snapshotted, meaning over 10 MB, promised files or unsupported types: the user is told before anything is written and chooses between proceeding without restore and copy-only.
- Focus moved to another application by delivery time: hold, and show a card with the text, Deliver and Copy. Re-activating the latched application first is opt-in, because it steals focus.
- Focus moved within the same application: deliver into the current element by default, under a per-mode toggle, matching the common case of clicking into the field while speaking.
- Latched application quit: hold and offer copy.
- Submit modifier: the Return is posted only when the modifier was held at stop, delivery went to the latched element, and the path posted events. A held or unconfirmed delivery never auto-submits.

## Service failures (D-003)

A service crash or termination invalidates the connection. The client marks the run failed at its current stage with the exit status, keeps every committed result, releases the job's credit, and offers retry. Three crashes on one model installation mark it suspect in the model list. Because a service holds only a loaded model and the current job's window queue, retry reloads from the manifest and needs no state salvage. A service that stops consuming credit is treated as hung after a no-progress interval measured against delivered windows, and is terminated by the client.

## Model and runtime failures (D-022)

- Download interrupted or hash mismatch: the staging directory is removed, no blob is created, the active installation is untouched, and the error names expected and computed digests.
- User-supplied model failing the load smoke test: it stays in staging with the error attached and nothing is activated. The smoke test checks that the runtime can load the weights and produce output on a fixed sample; it is a capability check and never a quality judgment, so a compatible model with no benchmark row activates normally and is labeled unmeasured.
- Model blob missing for a pinned run: the run fails at the stage that needed it and points at the model manager. Loading never falls back to downloading.
- Pairing exceeding the residency budget: refused at activation with the arithmetic shown, the refusal stating whether the numbers are measured or declared, and the user can override, because it is their machine.

## Resource and storage failures

- Disk full during capture: capture stops, the journal is sealed to the last complete chunk, the recording is marked interrupted, and the panel reports the reason.
- Journal fsync failing repeatedly: capture stops instead of continuing with an unrecoverable tail.
- Unsupported import format: the source is untouched, the session directory is removed, and the error names the format and the optional external decoder path (D-018, D-028).
- Audio device removed mid-run: capture stops and the recording is sealed as interrupted. The app does not silently switch devices under an active recording.

## Meeting attribution with weak evidence (D-023)

When the diarizer returns no calibrated probability, stored confidence is unknown and the segment's attribution_state is unverified. The transcript shows the cluster label with an unverified marker, and notes attribute only segments whose state is assigned or assigned_by_user. Segments whose microphone content correlates with delayed system audio are marked probable echo and excluded from microphone-side attribution. A user can assign, merge or split speakers at any time; manual assignment sets attribution_state to assigned_by_user, which no later diarization run overwrites.

## Desktop restore failures (D-025)

The app can observe that some audio client is running on the default output device and can post a play-pause key; neither identifies the application that reacted. Automatic resume is therefore off by default: after recording, the menu and panel offer Resume playback as a user action for ten minutes. When the user enables automatic resume, it fires only if the app posted the pause, the same output device is still default, the device is still idle, and under ten minutes have elapsed; the menu records that the app cannot confirm which application it addressed. Input device volume is restored only if the current value still equals the value the app set; any mismatch means no restore and a note that the setting was left as found.

## What this section covers

Task-level phases are produced after design acceptance. What belongs here is the ordering the design imposes, the evidence that closes each capability area, and the cost of the extensions the specification asks about. Every ordering constraint exists because a later decision depends on an earlier result, and every acceptance item names evidence in place of a completion claim.

## Evidence gates that precede frozen boundaries (D-034)

Four measurements can invalidate a boundary, so each runs before the boundary it could overturn.

- F1, runtime harness. Word error rate on a fixed corpus, time to final transcript, service peak resident size at 10 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours, cancellation latency at p50 and p95, and whether resuming from a window checkpoint reproduces the unpreempted transcript. It precedes freezing the scheduler's preemption policy (D-004) and the admission arithmetic of D-027, both of which currently run on conservative defaults. It also tests the chosen runtime against its fallback, so a negative result changes the adapter behind SpeechRecognizer and nothing above it (D-020).
- F2, service isolation. Load a model inside the sandboxed service, attempt an outbound connection and assert denial, attempt a write outside the job scratch directory and assert denial, and check whether a process the service spawns inherits the restriction. It precedes the entitlement set, the model-access path (descriptor passing against a read-only path exception) and the wording of the offline guarantee (D-028).
- F3, kill-at-offset capture. Kill the writer at randomized offsets across chunk boundaries and mid-fsync, recover, and record the maximum lost interval and any index corruption. It precedes asserting expected recovery outcomes for the capturing and sealing states (D-030, D-031).
- F4, insertion and pasteboard timing matrix. Selected-text insertion and paste with readback across the target applications listed under verification, recording whether existing content survives, whether a change is observable, and when each target reads the pasteboard. It precedes shipping per-application delivery profiles (D-009). The ladder itself does not wait on it, because its default for an unmeasured target is one unconfirmed attempt with deferred restore.

## Dependency order among capability areas

- The store, the run state machine, the manifest, the lease protocol and the recovery table depend on nothing external and come first, exercised against fake adapters. Everything else depends on them.
- Capture and delivery depend on the run machine, the recovery contract and the capability matrix (D-006, D-031, D-032). Neither depends on a model, so both can be accepted before any runtime is integrated.
- Recognition depends on capture and on the model store, because a run pins a model installation (D-022).
- Vocabulary and the Standard mode depend on recognition. Generation modes depend on vocabulary, on the validator packs (D-012) and on F2, which governs how the generation service is launched.
- Automatic mode selection and context depend on modes existing and on the permission matrix for their degraded states.
- System audio and file import depend on the ingest port and on the memory slope from F1, which tells the credit window how much a service will hold.
- Meetings depend on system-audio and file capture, on the diarizer decision (D-023) and on the acquisition path for weights the application does not bundle.
- Languages and retention depend on results and leases already existing; translation is a result kind and retention is a deletion job under the same protocol (D-033).
- Desktop integration depends on capture and delivery only.

## Acceptance evidence by area

Each area is accepted on evidence approved by the owner named in D-035, against behavior tables written before the tests.

- Store and run machine: the recovery outcome for every non-terminal state, asserted after a kill at that state boundary, matching the approved table.
- Capture: the measured loss bound from F3, plus a decodable artifact after every injected kill.
- Delivery: the dated application matrix from F4, automated permission-matrix tests, and a crash-during-delivery test showing needs_review with no re-post.
- Recognition: word error rate rows attached to machine, model revision and quantization, plus the memory slope at three durations measured inside the service.
- Vocabulary: table-driven determinism across ordering, boundaries, case and scripts without spaces.
- Modes: human rubric scores on the fidelity corpus including adversarial cases, and per-mode validator fallback rates.
- Models: crash injection between blob rename and the activation transaction, activation while a run holds a lease, an import with no benchmark row that activates and is labeled unmeasured, and a complete session with the network denied.
- Mode rules and context: a dated browser URL matrix and rule-shadowing tests.
- Input sources: resident size at 10 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours in both processes with the fitted slope reported, and a failed import leaving its source byte-identical.
- Meetings: two-stream alignment drift, diarization error rate on a labeled internal set, and the share of segments carrying unknown confidence.
- History: deletion and retention race tests against live leases, and provenance tests over two recognition runs of one recording.
- Desktop: a manual matrix over a music player, a browser tab and a video conferencing application, recording what paused and what resumed.

## Adding a new input source

A new source implements AudioSource, emitting timestamped native frames plus a SourceDescriptor giving live or seekable, clock domain, known duration, native rate and channel layout, and whether it honors credit. Only arming branches on live against seekable, because a live source latches a delivery target and a file source does not. The alternative considered was a pipeline per source, each owning its chunking, conversion and cancellation. That is shorter today and duplicates the parts most likely to be wrong: a memory bug on long input would exist only in the import path, and cancellation semantics would drift between paths. The cost of one port is that every source carries timing metadata even when it has one stream and no drift.

## Replacing a model runtime

Runtimes are separate adapter targets and separate service binaries, each publishing a capability descriptor with measured fields and a parameter schema. results.params_json stores parameters under a stable application-level schema with a runtime-specific extension blob, so History rows from an old runtime stay readable after a swap. The settings interface renders common parameters, meaning context length, temperature, beam size, thread count and quantization, generically from that schema, and a runtime may supply presentation hooks for parameters with conditional validity, model-specific ranges or memory effects. Replacing a runtime therefore adds a bounded amount of interface work; a claim that a schema removes bespoke interface work entirely would be too strong.

Calling a runtime API directly from feature code removes a layer. Under that arrangement, swapping runtimes touches every call site, the settings interface and the persisted parameters, and old History rows referencing removed parameter names become uninterpretable. RESEARCH flags long-recording behavior and integration cost as unexamined for both speech candidates, so designing as though the first choice is permanent would be the wrong bet.

Storage effect of a swap is bounded by the content-addressed blob store: each installation is referenced by rows naming a runtime kind, so the model manager shows per-runtime totals and can release a runtime's blobs once nothing references them.

## Maintenance costs accepted

- GRDB: a dependency with its own release cadence plus migration discipline, paid for by FTS5 and tested migrations.
- Vendored C and C++ runtimes: long builds, periodic vendoring and upstream API drift. Pinned to tagged revisions with an update checklist that reruns the evaluation harness and refreshes capability descriptors.
- CGEventTap and accessibility insertion: per-application behavior is undocumented and changes. The delivery matrix is re-run per macOS minor release and per major update of the applications in it, and the result is a dated table in the repository.
- Validator language packs: each language needs segmentation, interrogative detection and a content-word list, plus rubric review in that language. Languages without a pack take the fail-closed path.
- Chunk journal: extra file management, an fsync every chunk period and a sealer to maintain. It buys a recovery story that does not depend on a container surviving a kill.
- XPC services: four bundles to sign, entitlement sets to keep correct, and interruption handling in the client. A missing entitlement fails closed, which is the direction worth paying for.
- Media key posting: it can break silently. Manual resume as the default means a break degrades to nothing happening.

## What supporting other Macs would require

Intel support means the whisper.cpp adapter with its own model format, a smaller generation model, its own memory budget and its own evaluation run; RESEARCH notes that documented platform support does not establish comparable performance. Machines with 8 GB need a smaller pairing and a residency policy that unloads the speech model before loading the generation model, at the cost of latency between stages. Both are adapter and policy changes and neither touches the store or the run machine.

## Who decides what correct means (D-035)

A passing test shows the implementation met its assertions under the tested conditions; the assertions can encode a wrong expectation. Expected behavior is therefore written and approved before tests are written. docs/behavior/ holds a table per subsystem giving, for each state and event pair, the expected next state, the persisted effect and the user-visible effect. Cancellation, permission loss per capability, focus change, crash at each boundary, lease conflict, service interruption and validator fallback are events in those tables. Every row cites a SPEC.md clause; rows with no clause are marked derived and need explicit approval. The normative approver is the user as product owner, or a delegate named in docs/behavior/OWNERS; independent authorship is a hygiene rule and carries no authority. Tests reference row identifiers, and changing an approved row requires re-approval recorded in git history.

## Automated checks

- Run state machine property tests over every state and event pair including generated random sequences, asserting invariants: no delivery without a previously committed delivery_attempts row; no results row for a run cancelled before sealing; an artifact exists on disk exactly when its row says so; results.text is never updated; every non-recognition result has a derived_from_result_id belonging to the same recording.
- Provenance tests: re-recognize a recording under a second speech model, then rewrite and translate from each recognition result, and assert that every artifact resolves to exactly one recognition result and one model installation.
- Crash injection: SIGKILL at each stage boundary, relaunch, and assert the recovery outcome named in the approved table for that state, including no automatic re-delivery after a kill during delivering and idempotent re-sealing after a kill during sealing.
- Kill-at-offset capture experiment: randomized kills during capture across chunk boundaries and mid-fsync, measuring the maximum lost interval and asserting that container plus index always yields a decodable artifact. It replaces the earlier assumption that a truncated container can be finalized, and it has not been run.
- Deletion and retention races: a deterministic scheduler test that deletes a recording, and separately runs an age policy and an audio-discard policy, while a worker and a player hold leases; asserts that commits abort, no rows appear, scratch is removed, retention defers, and playback is not interrupted.
- Service isolation: from inside a running inference service, attempt an outbound connection to a remote host and to a listening local socket and assert both fail; attempt a write outside the job scratch directory and assert it fails; repeat from a process the service spawns. Secondary evidence comes from build checks that service targets and their dependency closure import no networking modules, a symbol scan of the linked binaries, and a static check that fails the build if a runtime is constructed through an initializer that can download.
- Offline session: a dictation, an import and a model load under a network-denied profile, asserting no failure and no attempted connection.
- Long-input memory: import at 10 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours, sampling resident size of the app and of the speech service across each run, asserting a per-duration ceiling and that the fitted slope of peak resident size against duration is within measurement noise. Measuring one duration in one process cannot establish that memory is independent of duration.
- Prompt-injection corpus: clipboard and screen context containing instruction-shaped text, asserting that the contract validator holds, the transcript survives, and no span of eight or more tokens present in context and absent from the transcript appears in the output.
- Validator language behavior: for each mode and language pair without a pack, assert the run falls back to the normalized transcript, records the reason, and delivers nothing unvalidated unless the per-mode override is set.
- Vocabulary determinism: ordering, ICU word boundaries, case handling, scripts without spaces and post-generation reapplication, table-driven.
- Model activation: crash injection between blob rename and the activation transaction, activation while a run holds a lease on the previous installation, garbage collection with and without live leases, and an import with no benchmark row asserting that activation succeeds and the interface labels quality unmeasured.
- Model notices: assert that every installed asset has a recorded license identifier and retained notice, and that the downloader refuses an asset whose notice is absent.
- Schema migration from fixture databases at each prior version.
- Panel placement restore across display reconfiguration, including a removed display and an off-screen frame.

## Human review where assertions are weak

Transformation fidelity is reviewed and not only asserted. A fixed corpus of recordings has expected outputs per mode, scored against a rubric: meaning preserved, no invented facts, questions still questions, vocabulary terms intact, formatting within the declared contract. The corpus includes adversarial cases built to pass lexical checks while changing meaning: removed or inserted negation, swapped quantities, modality changes such as must to may, swapped attribution between two named people, an answer appended after a retained question, and a sentence copied from the context block. Cross-language cases cover each shipped validator pack. The reviewer is not the author of the mode under review, and the approver of the expected outputs is the product owner.

Practical behavior in other macOS applications is verified by running the delivery matrix by hand across TextEdit, Mail, Notes, Safari plain input and contenteditable, Chrome, Xcode, Terminal, VS Code, Slack, Messages and Figma. Each cell records whether selected-text insertion is supported and whether it preserved existing field content; insertion at a caret in the middle of existing text; replacement of an active selection; paste with a delayed consumer; pasteboard restore outcome, including targets that read late and content that cannot be snapshotted; non-Latin text covering Japanese, Arabic in a right-to-left field, combining marks and emoji; behavior with an input method active; secure fields; and focus changing while events are being posted. The table is dated and re-run on macOS updates.

## Measurement protocols that have not been run

No benchmark here has been executed. Each protocol is defined so that results, when they exist, are attributable.

- Recognition: word error rate by language on a public set and an internal set, recording machine model, memory, macOS version, runtime revision, model revision and quantization, and audio characteristics. Recognition is scored separately from rewriting, because a rewrite rubric cannot distinguish a mis-recognized word from a badly reworded sentence.
- Latency: stop to delivered text, split into recognition and generation, at three durations, reported as a distribution over repeated runs.
- Runtime capability descriptors: cancellation latency at p50 and p95, transcript equivalence after preemption and resume, peak service resident size and Metal heap peak per model installation.
- Diarization: diarization error rate on a labeled internal meeting set, the share of segments carrying unknown confidence, whether clustering distance is monotone with correctness, and behavior under speaker echo when headphones are not used.
- Meeting notes: rubric scoring against the audio, with citation validity checked automatically and the uncited-bullet drop rate tracked.
- Two-stream alignment: drift between microphone and system streams over a long meeting, measured against injected reference tones.

Until a measurement exists, the interface reports language support as declared by the model publisher and marked unmeasured, and no latency claim appears in the product.
assumptions: Deployment baseline is macOS 14.0. Basis: RESEARCH records macOS 14 and Xcode 16 among the prerequisites of the Argmax Swift package selected in D-020, and ScreenCaptureKit system-audio capture predates 14, so nothing in the capture path needs a higher floor. Reconsider if the Argmax dependency is dropped, which lets the floor fall to whatever the remaining APIs need, or if measured two-stream drift forces the WWDC24 unified microphone and system stream, which raises the floor to macOS 15.

Apple Silicon with 16 GB is the evaluation target and Intel is unsupported in the first release. Basis: stated in the specification; RESEARCH notes whisper.cpp supports Intel, so a second adapter behind SpeechRecognizer keeps the option open without a structural change. Reconsider when an Intel requirement is confirmed; the work is a second adapter, a model pairing, a memory budget and a separate evaluation run.

The application ships outside the Mac App Store, unsandboxed, with hardened runtime and Developer ID notarization, containing sandboxed XPC services. Basis: setting selected text on other applications' accessibility elements and running a session-level event tap are unavailable to a sandboxed application without exceptions granted outside the App Store, while RESEARCH records that bundled services have their own sandboxes independent of the shell. Reconsider only through a distribution decision by the product owner; App Store distribution removes push-to-talk and the accessibility insertion path instead of merely changing them, which is why it is carried as the one blocking question.

A sandboxed XPC service with the network client entitlement withheld can load model weights and run Core ML and Metal inference, receiving weights as opened file descriptors or through a read-only path exception scoped to the models directory, and a process it spawns inherits the restriction. Basis: Apple's XPC guide describes per-service sandboxes and App Sandbox documents inheritance by child processes; neither has been verified for these runtimes here. Reconsider at gate F2. Fallback: an unsandboxed service with the network claim narrowed to structural absence plus a network-denied session test, and the external decoder left off by default.

Model residency fits an 8 GB application budget on the 16 GB target: a turbo-class speech model at roughly 0.8 to 1.6 GB of weights, an 8B-class generation model at 4-bit quantization at roughly 4.5 to 5 GB, and a few hundred MB of key-value cache at 8k context. Basis: published quantized file sizes and standard cache arithmetic, with no measured resident size and no accounting for runtime workspaces or Metal heaps. Reconsider at the first F1 descriptor, which reports process resident size and Metal peak; refusals state whether their numbers are measured or declared.

The maximum audio loss after an abrupt termination is one chunk period plus unflushed data within it. Basis: chunks are written, fsynced and renamed individually and the packet index is appended and fsynced, so recovery depends on records the application wrote itself instead of on a container surviving truncation. The exact bound has not been measured. Reconsider after the kill-at-offset experiment; a worse bound is answered by shortening the chunk period, which costs more fsyncs.

Prompt-based vocabulary biasing in the whisper family raises the chance a term is recognized and guarantees nothing. Basis: the mechanism is a decoder prompt instead of a decoding constraint, and the prompt slot is bounded at roughly 224 tokens. The product text says exactly that. Reconsider if a runtime exposes real biasing or constrained decoding, which moves exact-name handling into recognition.

Lexical and structural validator checks are necessary conditions on transformation fidelity and not a proof that a mode obeyed its contract. Basis: content-word recall, interrogative survival, expansion ratio and context n-gram overlap can all pass on text whose meaning changed. Reconsider if the adversarial fidelity corpus finds a class of violations that survives every check, which would argue for a sampled semantic check by a second model despite its cost and its shared failure mode.

A default 750 ms deferral before restoring the pasteboard is long enough for the common paste consumer. Basis: a conservative starting value with no measurement; the panel offers Restore now and per-application profiles override it. Reconsider from the F4 matrix, which records observed read delay per target; targets that read late get restore disabled instead of a longer timer.

A CoreAudio device-is-running flag on the default output device is an adequate trigger for offering to pause media and is not evidence of ownership. Basis: it is a public property needing no private framework, and it identifies neither the playing application nor the effect of a posted media key. That is why automatic resume is off by default. Reconsider if a supported API supplies target identity and confirms the pause transition.

AVFoundation covers the initial import format matrix: wav, aiff, caf, mp3, m4a in AAC and ALAC, mp4, m4v and mov. Basis: system decoder coverage. Reconsider at the first refusal, with opus in webm or matroska the likely ones, at which point the user-selected external decoder running inside the sandboxed decode service is the documented path.

FTS5 is compiled into the system SQLite on the deployment baseline. Basis: it has shipped enabled for several macOS releases, though this is a build-setup check and not a verified fact here. Reconsider immediately if the check fails; the fallback is GRDB against a bundled SQLite, which increases binary size and adds an update obligation.

Separate microphone and system-audio streams give better attribution than diarizing a mixed stream, and channel origin is a fact about capture instead of a claim about who spoke. Basis: structural, since the two capture paths exist and channel origin is certain, while echo from speakers into the microphone is not accounted for by structure alone. Reconsider after diarization and echo evaluation; if a mixed-stream diarizer performs comparably, the second stream becomes an optimization.

The clustering threshold exposed by the selected diarizer is not a calibrated probability that a speaker label is correct. Basis: stated in RESEARCH for SpeakerKit's configuration. The schema therefore records clustering distance and margin as evidence and stores calibrated confidence as unknown when the runtime supplies none. Reconsider if evaluation shows the distance is monotone with correctness on the internal set, which would allow a derived threshold with its calibration curve recorded alongside it.

Lossless 16 kHz mono audio at roughly 50 to 60 MB per hour makes indefinite dictation retention acceptable by default, while native-rate meeting streams are large enough to surface in the library size view. Basis: arithmetic from 16-bit PCM at 115 MB per hour and typical lossless ratios. Reconsider when a library crosses a user-visible size threshold, at which point the retention interface is surfaced instead of a default quietly applied.

A 200 ms arming budget is tolerable before speech starts, and context sources missing it are skipped for that run. Basis: a design choice about perceived responsiveness with no user study. Reconsider if screen-context sampling routinely misses the deadline and users want it, which moves sampling off the arming path and makes the rewrite stage wait for it.

Weights the application offers for download are limited to assets whose notices permit redistribution, and everything else is user-imported. Basis: RESEARCH records the WhisperKit model card as MIT and records component-specific notices for the diarization collection referring to WeSpeaker and VBx. Reconsider per asset as the notice inventory is compiled; an asset that cannot be offered stays importable, so no feature depends on the outcome.

decisions.title: macOS baseline and hardware target
decisions.choice: Deployment target macOS 14.0 and Apple Silicon for the first release, with later-OS APIs gated at runtime and never required.
decisions.rationale: The speech runtime selected in D-020 is distributed in a Swift package whose prerequisites RESEARCH records as macOS 14 and Xcode 16, so the floor follows a dependency the design has committed to instead of an unselected one. ScreenCaptureKit system-audio capture is available at 14; the WWDC24 microphone stream output arrived later, and microphone capture uses AVAudioEngine on every supported version, so the newer output is off the critical path. The specification names Apple Silicon with 16 GB as the evaluation target.

alternatives.option: Baseline macOS 15 for the unified ScreenCaptureKit microphone and system-audio stream
alternatives.tradeoff: One capture path and a shared clock for meetings, at the cost of excluding Sonoma users for a convenience the two-stream design handles with host-time alignment.

alternatives.option: Baseline macOS 13
alternatives.tradeoff: Wider reach; falls below the selected runtime's stated prerequisite and adds an operating system to the support matrix that nothing is evaluated on.

alternatives.option: Ship Intel and Apple Silicon together
alternatives.tradeoff: Broader hardware coverage; doubles the evaluation burden that RESEARCH warns documentation cannot substitute for, and forces a second model tier before the primary target is measured.

decisions.consequences: Meetings align two streams by host time instead of receiving them from one. Intel users wait for the second speech adapter and its own evaluation. Any API newer than 14 sits behind an availability check with a defined fallback, and the availability matrix is part of the capture behavior tables.
decisions.reconsider_when: The Argmax dependency is dropped, measured two-stream drift forces a single-stream capture path, or an Intel requirement is confirmed.

decisions.title: Package layout and dependency direction
decisions.choice: One SPM package with a pure core, a ports target of protocols and value types, a validation target holding transformation contracts and language packs, adapter targets per external concern, service targets for inference, and a thin Xcode app shell as the composition root. Core depends only on ports; nothing depends on an adapter except the shell.
decisions.rationale: The scope includes a speech runtime that may be replaced, four input sources, and an insertion mechanism whose behavior varies per target application. Each is an adapter. Keeping the run state machine, mode resolution, the vocabulary pipeline and contract validation free of system frameworks is what lets the earliest work exercise cancel, crash, delete-during-processing and retention races before any runtime exists. Service logic living in library targets keeps it inside swift test even though the bundles are produced by Xcode.

alternatives.option: Single application target with feature folders
alternatives.tradeoff: Faster early progress; every behavioral test then needs permissions and real models, and swapping a runtime touches feature code throughout.

alternatives.option: Separate SPM packages per subsystem in a workspace
alternatives.tradeoff: Stronger boundaries and independent versioning, at the cost of cross-package version churn for a single application with one consumer.

decisions.consequences: Adapters need explicit wiring in the shell and value types at the boundary in place of framework types passed around. The application bundle cannot come from swift build alone, so there are two entry points: swift test for logic and the Xcode scheme for the shipping application and its signed services.
decisions.reconsider_when: The port boundary starts needing per-adapter escape hatches that leak framework types into core, which would mean the abstraction is fighting the domain.

decisions.title: Inference runs in bundled sandboxed XPC services
decisions.choice: Speech recognition, generation and optional external decoding each run in a bundled XPC service, sandboxed on its own with com.apple.security.network.client withheld, reached over its XPC connection. Model weights arrive as opened file descriptors or through a read-only path exception scoped to Models/blobs. No inference runs in the app process and nothing listens on a port.
decisions.rationale: RESEARCH's follow-up records that bundled services have separate sandboxes, that a service can fail or be terminated independently of its client, and that signed services with network entitlements withheld are the thing to evaluate for inference; it also states that a scan for socket symbols cannot establish that a process lacks network access. A withheld entitlement is a property of the process, so it covers linked frameworks and dynamically loaded code that a scan cannot reach. Crash isolation is the second reason: a quantization that faults a runtime should not take the in-flight transcript with it. Residency accounting is the third: model memory lives in a process the app can measure and terminate.

alternatives.option: Child helper processes over an inherited socket pair
alternatives.tradeoff: Full control of launch and lifecycle with no launchd involvement; provides no system-level egress denial, so the offline claim reduces to the symbol scan RESEARCH rejects as evidence.

alternatives.option: Link the runtimes into the application process
alternatives.tradeoff: Lowest latency and no serialization boundary; a native crash kills the app mid-run and address-space growth from model loading persists for the process lifetime.

alternatives.option: Run the upstream HTTP server on localhost
alternatives.tradeoff: Reuses upstream tooling and its API; opens a port every local process can reach and turns the offline property into a claim about configuration the app does not own.

decisions.consequences: Connection interruption is a normal event: the run fails at its stage, committed results stand, and the next admission rebuilds the service. Audio windows cross the connection under credit, so the memory ceiling is measured in the service as well as the app. Model file access needs descriptors or a path exception, settled by F2. Four bundles are signed with their own entitlement sets, and a missing entitlement fails closed.
decisions.reconsider_when: F2 shows a sandboxed service cannot load the chosen runtimes, or IPC overhead measurably dominates generation latency for short dictations.

decisions.title: Concurrency model and resource scheduling from measured runtime capabilities
decisions.choice: One actor per processing run owning its state and rows; a real-time audio callback writing into lock-free rings; a single ResourceScheduler actor with capture, interactive and batch lanes admitting at most one speech job and one generation job. Preemption policy is read from each runtime's measured capability descriptor: yield at a safe checkpoint where the runtime supports it, otherwise cancel and restart from the last committed checkpoint, or let the batch job finish behind a displayed bound. Until descriptors exist, use cancel-and-restart.
decisions.rationale: The scope puts a latency-sensitive dictation path beside long batch work on a machine that cannot hold several models resident, so an admission policy is needed and is better in one testable place than invented by the first task that hits contention. Nothing in RESEARCH establishes that either runtime can checkpoint and resume without changing output, so resumability is a measured descriptor field and the conservative default is correct whichever way it comes out.

alternatives.option: Unstructured concurrency with a global lock around model access
alternatives.tradeoff: Less code; priority inversion when a three-hour import holds the lock while the user dictates, with no clean preemption point.

alternatives.option: Serial queue, first come first served
alternatives.tradeoff: Predictable; the user waits behind a batch job, which is the failure the requirements care about most.

alternatives.option: Concurrent speech and generation residency with no admission control
alternatives.tradeoff: Better pipelining on a large machine; on the 16 GB target it invites swap, turning a latency problem into a system-wide stall.

decisions.consequences: Batch workers need resumable checkpoints under either policy, since cancel-and-restart still needs a restart point. The provisional pass is an admitted job that can be denied, so the panel has a preview-paused state. The audio callback thread has hard constraints that need review discipline. Descriptor values become shipped data refreshed when a runtime is updated.
decisions.reconsider_when: Descriptors show a runtime whose resume reproduces the unpreempted transcript, allowing true preemption, or measurements show a machine class where concurrent residency fits and the single-job rule costs latency for nothing.

decisions.title: Persistence: SQLite with FTS5 for metadata and text, files for audio
decisions.choice: SQLite through GRDB in WAL mode for metadata, runs, results, leases and result text, with FTS5 over result text; audio in per-recording directories. Numbered migrations with fixture-based migration tests.
decisions.rationale: History requires search across transcripts and results, and FTS5 with bm25 ranking and snippets is the reason to prefer SQLite. Deletion during active work, lease acquisition and model activation all need a transaction that combines a check with a write. Keeping audio out of the database keeps its backup, integrity check and migration times short.

alternatives.option: SwiftData
alternatives.tradeoff: Least code for models and views with native observation; no full-text index, and migration behavior is harder to test against fixtures for a schema that must survive many capability additions.

alternatives.option: Core Data with an external search index
alternatives.tradeoff: Mature and Apple-supported; adds a second index to keep consistent with deletions, which is the consistency problem the tombstone and lease rules exist to contain.

alternatives.option: Raw libsqlite3 with a hand-written wrapper
alternatives.tradeoff: No third-party dependency; reimplements migrations, statement caching and observation, which is where maintenance accumulates.

alternatives.option: JSON files per recording with an in-memory index
alternatives.tradeoff: Inspectable and easy to back up; search, leases and transactional deletion become bespoke, and the index is rebuilt every launch.

decisions.consequences: A dependency with its own release cadence and migration discipline. FTS triggers must stay in sync with result inserts and deletes, covered by tests. Database and files can disagree after a crash, which the recovery contract resolves.
decisions.reconsider_when: The system SQLite lacks FTS5 on the baseline, in which case GRDB is built against a bundled SQLite, or library sizes make a per-recording file layout with an external index preferable.

decisions.title: Processing runs as explicit state machines with a per-run settings snapshot
decisions.choice: A state machine per processing run (idle, arming, capturing, sealing, recognizing, refining, rewriting, delivering, terminal) in the pure core, with a RunManifest written and fsynced at run start pinning mode revision, model installation ids, vocabulary revision, language setting, translation flag, validator pack and, for reprocessing, the parent result id. Capture stages belong only to runs that capture.
decisions.rationale: Component boundaries follow this sequence. The manifest is what makes settings snapshots real: a run reads its manifest and never live settings, so editing a mode or switching models mid-run cannot change what a result means. The same manifest is what a reprocess copies and mutates, and what recovery reads after a crash. Attaching the machine to a run instead of to a recording is what lets one recording carry several recognitions without ambiguity.

alternatives.option: Read live settings at each stage
alternatives.tradeoff: No snapshot machinery; a mode edit during a long recognition silently changes the result's meaning, which the requirements forbid.

alternatives.option: Implicit state through nullable columns
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer types; illegal states become representable and per-stage cancellation loses its single definition point.

alternatives.option: One state machine per recording
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler list view; a second recognition has nowhere to live and reprocessing has to mutate the recording's state.

decisions.consequences: Every new capability declares where it sits in the sequence and what cancellation there means. Settings changes take effect on the next run, which the interface must show so it does not read as a bug. History shows runs, which is more structure in the detail view than a flat result list.
decisions.reconsider_when: A requirement needs mid-run settings changes, such as switching language during a long meeting, which would need a segmented manifest in place of one per run.

decisions.title: Cancellation contract defined per run stage
decisions.choice: A stage-indexed table of cancellation effects enforced in core and shown in the panel: arming discards everything; capturing discards the journal by default with an opt-in to seal it as interrupted; recognizing keeps audio and saves no partial transcript; refining drops the normalized result; rewriting keeps the normalized result and offers it; delivering is cancellable only before the first event is posted. Cancelling a reprocess run leaves every earlier run's results intact.
decisions.rationale: The specification requires defined effects at every processing stage. Two judgment calls carry the design: recognizing saves no partial transcript because a truncated transcript that looks complete is more damaging than an absent one, and rewriting keeps the normalized result because the expensive work is done and the user usually still wants their words.

alternatives.option: Cancel always discards everything
alternatives.tradeoff: One rule; throws away a completed recognition because the user did not want the rewrite, which is the most common late cancel.

alternatives.option: Cancel always keeps everything
alternatives.tradeoff: Nothing is lost; a sentence spoken into the wrong window persists to History, which is a privacy surprise.

alternatives.option: Prompt at cancel time
alternatives.tradeoff: No wrong default; a modal on the escape path is when a user least wants a dialog.

decisions.consequences: Workers need checkpoints so cancel is prompt without being abrupt. The panel needs a per-stage message so the effect is visible when it happens instead of discovered later in History.
decisions.reconsider_when: Usage shows repeated re-recording after cancels during recognition, which would argue for keeping partial transcripts clearly marked as partial.

decisions.title: Delivery target latched at arming with an explicit focus-change policy
decisions.choice: At arming, latch the frontmost process id, bundle identifier, window number, focused accessibility element and that element's insertion capability. At delivery: the same element delivers; the same application with a different element delivers by default under a per-mode toggle; a different application holds and shows a card with Deliver and Copy; a departed application holds. Re-focusing the latched target is opt-in. Only capture-initiated dictation runs deliver; reprocessing runs never auto-deliver.
decisions.rationale: The intended target is the one the user was looking at when they started speaking, and the panel is non-activating (D-011) so showing it does not disturb the latch. Holding instead of inserting into an unexpected application is conservative for a good reason: text placed in the wrong window can be unrecoverable and can be sensitive, while a hold costs one click.

alternatives.option: Always deliver into whatever is frontmost at delivery time
alternatives.tradeoff: No held results; text lands in the wrong application whenever focus changes during processing, which is common on longer recognitions.

alternatives.option: Always re-activate the latched application
alternatives.tradeoff: Matches intent most of the time; pulls focus away from whatever the user chose to do next, sometimes seconds later.

alternatives.option: Always hold and require confirmation
alternatives.tradeoff: Never wrong; adds a click to every dictation, which defeats the tool.

decisions.consequences: The panel needs a held state with actions and History must show undelivered results. The same-application default will occasionally insert into a different field in the same window, which is accepted because it matches clicking into the target field while speaking.
decisions.reconsider_when: Holds fire often enough to annoy, which would argue for making opt-in re-focus the default for users who enable it, or for shortening processing so focus changes are rarer.

decisions.title: Insertion ladder defined by caret and selection, with named observable signals
decisions.choice: Rung 1 sets AXSelectedText on the latched element, inserting at the caret or replacing the current selection, confirmed by reading back the selected-text range or value length. AXValue is never set. Rung 2 writes the pasteboard and posts Command-V; where the target exposes readable value or range state, sample before and after and wait up to 500 ms, treating an observed change as delivered and an observed absence as rejected. Rung 3, synthesized Unicode typing capped at 400 characters, runs only after an observed rejection. When the target exposes no readable state, the paste outcome is recorded posted_unconfirmed, nothing further is attempted, and the panel offers Copy and Deliver again. Pasteboard restore happens after the outcome is determined, only while the change count is ours, deferred by a per-application profile delay of 750 ms by default for unconfirmed outcomes, and disabled for targets measured to read the pasteboard late.
decisions.rationale: RESEARCH distinguishes an accessibility object's value from its selected text and notes that setting an editable field's value can replace its contents, so insertion is expressed as a selection-aware operation. It also states that posting a paste event supplies no general acknowledgment that the target consumed the clipboard, so the ladder splits targets into readable and unreadable: readable targets give a signal that makes both the fallthrough and the restore safe, and unreadable targets get a single attempt with no retry, which is the only behavior that cannot duplicate text.

alternatives.option: Pasteboard and Command-V only
alternatives.tradeoff: One path to maintain; always disturbs the pasteboard, including where selected-text insertion would be clean and confirmable.

alternatives.option: Synthetic typing only
alternatives.tradeoff: Never touches the pasteboard; slow for long text, drops characters under load in some targets, and interleaves badly with user typing.

alternatives.option: A dedicated input method
alternatives.tradeoff: The system-supported route for inserting text, avoiding both the pasteboard and event synthesis; requires the user to install and select an input method, changing their typing setup for a dictation feature.

alternatives.option: Keep a fixed short restore delay
alternatives.tradeoff: Simple and usually invisible; races targets that read the pasteboard after the delay, pasting whatever the app restored.

decisions.consequences: Per-application profiles become shipped data with a maintenance obligation and a dated matrix. Some targets will never confirm delivery, so posted_unconfirmed is a normal outcome the interface must explain instead of an error. Restore is best-effort and says when it was skipped.
decisions.reconsider_when: The F4 prototype finds a readable signal for targets currently classed unreadable, or a supported API for inserting text into another application appears.

decisions.title: Delivery idempotency and no automatic retry
decisions.choice: Commit a delivery_attempts row naming recording, result, run, target and state before posting any event. States are pending, posted, posted_unconfirmed, held and failed. On launch, pending, posted and posted_unconfirmed become needs_review. The app never re-posts automatically; re-delivery is a user action.
decisions.rationale: Paste into an unreadable target gives no confirmation, so after a crash the app cannot distinguish delivered from about to deliver. Any automatic retry risks inserting the same paragraph twice into someone's document. Committing the attempt before posting means recovery always sees that an attempt was in flight, and needs_review surfaces it without acting.

alternatives.option: Retry pending deliveries on launch
alternatives.tradeoff: Recovers a crash before posting; duplicates text after posting, with no way to tell the cases apart.

alternatives.option: No attempt record, recover from run state
alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer table; the window between deciding to deliver and posting is exactly where a crash is unrecoverable without a durable record.

alternatives.option: Confirm by reading the target back for every path
alternatives.tradeoff: Would allow safe retry; unavailable in the targets that need the paste path most, so it cannot be the general rule.

decisions.consequences: After a crash mid-delivery the user gets a needs_review item and decides. Re-delivery is always explicit, one extra interaction in a rare case.
